items.title: Eddie Marshall interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: Anyway well I heard Miles Davis and that did it. I was totally gone for jazz.

ctx.x: Didn’t they have a long bar, a long stage behind the bar or something.

Yeah, yeah, yeah. It was, I don’t know, anyhow so I started playing with Cookie and the Seven Sharps and Cookie is still alive, he’s like eighty something years old. And that was it. And I Just stayed with that until I was 18. And then I had an uncle, my Uncle Roddy, who got drafted into the Army. Actually he got drafted into the Marines during the Korean War which was really — I think he was drafted and they gave him a choice or something. But he ended up a draftee in the Marines. And he was a jazz fanatic. So…
That’s so interesting that you got pulled out of your father’s mode into this thing, and then out of that thing. © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
